A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QTALE framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy, perplexity, latency, routing, ablation, and instruction-following results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds routing diagnostics, a controlled layer-skipping experiment, larger-batch latency measurements, and GSM8K evaluation.

M1.justification: The entropy-regularized training objective, router, inference threshold mechanism, and two-stage calibration remain unchanged. Equation 9 corrects a subscript to match the existing verbal routing rule; the newly documented batching and kernel implementation does not establish a redesigned algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix B.7 adds GSM8K evaluation with generated chain-of-thought mathematical reasoning, extending the task requirements beyond the previously reported evaluations. The existing commonsense, MMLU, Alpaca, SAMSum, and AlpacaEval coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain their comparators, including full execution, D-LLM, SLEB, and alternative threshold-search methods. The new GSM8K and batch-size comparisons reuse full execution and D-LLM. The mixed-precision table renames the unchanged LoRA row to Full.

E3.justification: Existing experimental settings are retained. Added protocols include latency testing at batch sizes 8, 16, and 32; a 150-sample ARCe cosine-similarity experiment forcing layer 23 to be skipped; and GSM8K chain-of-thought evaluation with 64 calibration samples instead of the 300 used elsewhere.

E4.justification: v4 substantially expands the diagnostic evidence. Appendix A.4 supplements the selected-layer routing plots with flipping ratios averaged over layers 16–31 across four tasks and epochs 6–9. Appendix A.5 adds a controlled quantization/skipping comparison, while B.2 tests practical speedup across larger batches. Earlier ablations and sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these experiments. The added tables report point estimates and averages without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All 16 original tables retain their numerical values after matching renumbered counterparts. v4 adds substantial new findings in Tables 9, 10, 12, and 20: higher late-training flipping ratios, cosine similarity of 0.8605 versus 0.8219 when executing versus skipping under quantization, larger-batch latency results, and GSM8K results. For example, 4-bit LLaMA3.2-3B achieves 23.28% with QTALE versus 16.98% with D-LLM; this is a new comparison, not an improvement over a v1 GSM8K result.

T1.justification: Appendix A.5 introduces the additive error formulation e_total = e_skip + e_quant, without a formal proof. Equation 9 also corrects the bypass condition from p_l,1 < theta to p_l,0 < theta, making its branches consistent with the stated execution rule.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same two contributions and the claim of combining reduced FLOPs and memory with a CommonsenseQA accuracy gap below 0.5%. Removing 'no noticeable accuracy difference' from the abstract does not change the retained quantitative claim.

C2.justification: v4 adds an error-budget explanation in which executing more layers reduces skipping error to compensate for quantization. Appendix B.2 additionally explains padding-related latency and identifies kernel-launch overhead and control-flow inefficiencies as limits on realizing theoretical FLOPs savings. Existing redundancy interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 newly documents static batching, padding-token handling, gathering active tokens into dense inputs, and custom Triton routing and fused normalization/activation kernels. These improve implementation disclosure without establishing when those implementation choices were introduced. Existing training and calibration details remain.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning remain unchanged. Updates to entries such as GPTQ and ShortGPT concern publication venues, dates, and bibliographic formatting rather than new references or revised novelty claims.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v4 reorganizes the appendix into QTALE Details and Additional Evaluation, makes limited wording and terminology edits, corrects author information, and adds acknowledgments and an impact statement.

P2.justification: v4 adds four compact tables, relocates existing displays, adjusts spacing and table emphasis, and replaces the template running header. Figure 1 is visually refreshed, and Figure 4(a) corrects the reversed epoch 0 and epoch 6 labels. Existing plots and table structures otherwise remain largely intact.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens validation through GSM8K, broader routing diagnostics, controlled skipping analysis, and larger-batch latency measurements. Corrections to Equation 9 and Figure 4(a), together with kernel implementation details, improve clarity and reproducibility. The gain is limited because v1 already contains extensive evaluation, the central results remain unchanged, and the new additive error formulation is not formally established by the narrow cosine-similarity experiment.
